answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-bound reputation: every identity locks a deposit that is slashed when peers prove fraud, and only identities with a long, checkable work history earn high-value trades. Like a nebula condensing into stars, scattered interactions gather into one verifiable record. To forge a trusted army, an attacker must fund many long-lived histories, and one exposed fraud burns the whole stake, so reaching the zenith of trust costs far more than any single scam can repay.
